> I agree if this applies to HTML injection. Sanitising input before logging it does not make sense. If someone submits `<script>alert(1)` in a form, you want to exactly that to show up in the log, in order to investigate attacks.

For that you have requirement V5.3.3

> However, the application should protect against log injection. If lines are logged into a plain text file, newlines in user input should be escaped by the application before writing it to the log, to prevent attackers from injecting new log lines.

For that you have requirement V7.3.1
